full_judgment: 8. With regard to the question whether Mrs Azra Zaman Chowdhury did acquire any lawful title in the house at 19, New Eskaton Road, admittedly the house in question was acquired long-before the Independence of Bangladesh by the mother of Mrs. Azra Zaman Chowdhury who continued to reside in Pakistan even after the independence of Bangladesh as such. It, however appeared that in July, 1970 the mother of  Mrs. Azra Zaman Chowdhury had gifted away the house in question to her daughter, Mrs. Azra Zaman Chowdhury being one of the heirs, successors and legal representatives in due course according to law. An Affidavit sworn before the Commissioner of Affidavit at Karachi, in Pakistan on 11th July, 1970 by the mother of Mrs. Azra Zaman Chowdhury confirming the oral gift of the house in question accompanied by delivery of possession made on 12th July, 1978 at Dacca was produced before this Court A further affidavit affirmed before a 1st Class Magistrate at Dacca on 31st January, 1977 by Mr. Habibur Rahman and Mr. A.S.M Solaiman, being witness to the aforesaid gift was also produced before this Court. On consideration of such Affidavits and in view of the fact that under Muslim Personal Law oral gift accompanied by delivery of possession in presence of the witnessess is permissible, this Court accepted the right, title and interest of Mrs. Azra Zaman Chowdhury in the house at 19, New Eskaton Road, Dacca. That there has not been any mutation of name in various record with regard to the aforesaid house in favour of Mrs. Azra Zaman Chowdhury by itself will not disentitle her to claim legal ownership of the house in question, if she has otherwise acquired a valid title in the said house. In the aforesaid circumstances when this Court accepted the right, title an interest of Azra Zaman Chowdhury in the house at 19, New Eskaton Road, this by itself his created an affirmative presumption of title in favour of Azra Zaman Chowdhury which can every well be negative and rebutted by any other persons other than the allottees and tenants, claiming better title on such house, in an appropriate legal proceedings before an appropriate Civil Court.
